paper_metadata.title: CodeKGC: Code Language Model for Generative Knowledge Graph Construction
paper_metadata.abstract: CodeKGC formulates generative knowledge-graph construction as code completion: it converts text and target triples into Python-like code, uses schema-aware prompts based on class definitions, and optionally generates rationales before triples. The paper evaluates the approach against textual prompting and UIE on ADE, CoNLL04, and SciERC in zero-shot and few-shot settings.

problem_addressed: Generative knowledge graph construction from unstructured natural-language text, specifically extraction of relational triples while reducing the difficulty that flattened serializations have with structural dependencies, overlapping facts, and long-range relations.

methodology.primary_family: Zero-shot and few-shot LLM prompting (without task-specific model training)
secondary_families: Instruction-tuned or fine-tuned LLM methods (smaller-model experiment)
methodology.description: Execution pipeline: (1) use a predefined Python-conformant script to convert input text T and gold/output triple graph G into code-format Tc and Gc; (2) construct a schema-aware prompt with Entity, Relation, Triple, and Extract classes, where entity/relation types inherit from base classes; (3) append k in-context completed examples, optionally including rationales; (4) generate a rationale that first identifies candidate relations and then corresponding entities; (5) generate Extract([Triple(...)]) code; and (6) convert generated code back to triples/graph G. The main large-model runs use text-davinci-002 or text-davinci-003, with code-davinci-002 in ablations.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: Uses a predefined KG schema as prompt-time structural guidance, rather than discovering an ontology. Python base classes Entity and Relation encode entity/relation definitions; typed subclasses and Triple instances represent permitted graph structure, including entity-type constraints.

We further define Triple class ... Each triple will be represented as the instance of their corresponding entity and relation type classes.

input_output.input_type: Unstructured natural-language sentences, transformed into Python-like code prompts with natural-language docstrings, schema class definitions, and optionally in-context demonstration/rationale code.
input_output.input_granularity: Sentence-level examples; the paper describes each task instance as one text input T and its triple graph G.
input_output.output_representation: Typed relational triples encoded as Python-like Extract([Triple(head entity, relation, tail entity), ...]) code, then converted back into a knowledge graph/triple set.

datasets: ADE: adverse-drug-event texts; 1 adverse-effect relation and 2 entity types (disease, drug); 300 randomly selected test samples evaluated because of API-time constraints
SciERC: scientific-paper information extraction; 7 relations and 6 entity types
T-REx: 838,821 sentences, 4,378,318 triples, 10,496 relations (smaller-model code pre-training)
TEKGEN: 6,310,061 sentences, 10,609,697 triples, 1,013 relations (smaller-model code pre-training)
KELM: 15,616,551 sentences, 35,117,608 triples, 59,904 relations (smaller-model code pre-training)

metrics: Relation strict micro F1; a predicted triple is correct only when head entity, tail entity, and relation all exactly match. Entity types are predicted but excluded from F1.
baselines: Smaller-model comparisons: pre-trained/not-pre-trained T5 and CodeT5
evaluation.setting: Zero-shot and few-shot relation-extraction/knowledge-graph-construction evaluation on ADE, CoNLL04, and SciERC. Zero-shot replaces one-shot relations with synonyms; few-shot uses three-shot relation demonstrations. Results average three runs. Temperature is 0.5, max_tokens is 256 or 512, and generation stops at special patterns such as triple quotes, class, or #. ADE analyses also vary 1/5/10/15 in-context examples and evaluate a sampled overlapping-triple hard subset; a separate supervised smaller-model ADE study pre-trains for three days on four Tesla V100 GPUs.

value: Table 2 zero-shot relation-strict micro F1: CodeKGC/text-davinci-003 scores 43.7 on ADE, 41.6 on CoNLL04, and 19.5 on SciERC; CodeKGC/text-davinci-002 scores 42.5, 35.8, and 15.0, respectively.
Table 2 few-shot relation-strict micro F1: CodeKGC/text-davinci-003 scores 64.2 on ADE, 49.6 on CoNLL04, and 24.7 on SciERC; CodeKGC/text-davinci-002 scores 61.5, 42.7, and 18.5.
In few-shot mode, CodeKGC/text-davinci-003 exceeds its matched Vanilla Prompt by 5.4 F1 on ADE, 6.4 on CoNLL04, and 5.9 on SciERC. It also exceeds UIE on all three few-shot results in Table 2.

On CoNLL04 prompt-variation experiments, Figure 5 reports that both schema-aware prompting and rationale-enhanced generation improve CodeKGC relative to their ablations; the paper warns that lengthy rationale prompts can hurt when sample size is too small.
For the smaller-model ADE study, Figure 8 shows restructured-code-pretrained T5 at 75.6 and CodeT5 at 68.6 F1, below UIE at 81.1; non-pretrained models score 58.8 (T5) and 52.2 (CodeT5).

value: Author claim: schema-aware Python-format prompts explicitly represent entity, relation, property, and constraint structure through class definitions and typed triple instances.

Experimental result: the large-model CodeKGC prompt consistently exceeds its matched Vanilla Prompt in the Table 2 few-shot setting and improves zero-shot results on every reported dataset/backbone pair.
Experimental result: code formatting helps on long-range and overlapping-triple cases when paired with a strong code model; Figure 7 provides qualitative examples.

Review-level inference: representing schema and triples in an executable-style, typed code syntax makes the generated output easier to parse deterministically than unconstrained free-form text, provided the generated code follows the prescribed template.

value: Author-reported experimental finding: ADE performance is limited because the medical corpus contains many acronyms; in zero-shot mode CodeKGC is similar to Vanilla Prompt.

Author-reported limitation: performance on complex structures depends heavily on a powerful code-pretrained backbone; CodeKGC/text-davinci-002 can underperform Vanilla Prompt/text-davinci-002 on sampled hard examples.
Experimental result: the 770M restructured-code-pretrained models remain below UIE on ADE (best 75.6 versus UIE 81.1).

Review-level inference: the approach requires predefined entity and relation schemas and hand-designed code prompts, so transfer to a new schema needs schema encoding and prompt/example preparation rather than being fully schema-free.
